question: How many questions are there in the Life in the UK test?
sourceFact: 1.4: 'The test consists of 24 questions about important aspects of life in the UK.'

question: What level of English does the Life in the UK test assume?
sourceFact: 1.2: 'The questions are written in a way that requires an understanding of the English language at ESOL Entry Level 3.'

question: From October 2013, what evidence must you produce alongside passing the Life in the UK test for settlement or permanent residence?
options: Evidence of speaking and listening skills in English at B1 of the Common European Framework of Reference
sourceFact: 1.2: 'Produce acceptable evidence of speaking and listening skills in English at B1 of the Common European Framework of Reference. This is equivalent to ESOL Entry Level 3.'

question: Which of these is one of the fundamental principles of British life listed in the handbook?
sourceFact: 1.3: 'The fundamental principles of British life include: Democracy, The rule of law, Individual liberty, Tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs, Participation in community life.'

question: Select TWO things the UK offers in return for residents respecting and obeying the law.
options: A right to a fair trial
sourceFact: 1.3: 'In return, the UK offers: freedom of belief and religion, freedom of speech, freedom from unfair discrimination, a right to a fair trial, a right to join in the election of a government.'

question: As part of the citizenship ceremony, new citizens pledge to do what?
options: Uphold the UK's democratic values and observe its laws faithfully
sourceFact: 1.3: 'I will give my loyalty to the United Kingdom and respect its rights and freedoms. I will uphold its democratic values. I will observe its laws faithfully and fulfil my duties and obligations as a British citizen.'

question: In which languages, besides English, can special arrangements be made to take the Life in the UK test?
sourceFact: 1.4: 'The Life in the UK test is usually taken in English, although special arrangements can be made if you wish to take it in Welsh or Scottish Gaelic.'

question: True or false: you can take the Life in the UK test at any test centre of your choosing, including ones not registered with the UK Border Agency.
sourceFact: 1.4: 'You should not take your test at any other establishment as the UK Border Agency will only accept certificates from registered test centres.'

question: What ancient monument, still standing in Wiltshire, was probably a gathering place for seasonal ceremonies in the Stone Age?
sourceFact: 3.7: 'One of these monuments, Stonehenge, still stands in what is now the English county of Wiltshire. Stonehenge was probably a special gathering place for seasonal ceremonies.'

question: Who led the Roman invasion of Britain in AD 43?
sourceFact: 3.7: 'Julius Caesar led a Roman invasion of Britain in 55 BC. This was unsuccessful... In AD 43 the Emperor Claudius led the Roman army in a new invasion.'

question: Boudicca was the queen of which tribe, who fought against the Romans?
sourceFact: 3.7: 'One of the tribal leaders who fought against the Romans was Boudicca, the queen of the Iceni in what is now eastern England.'

question: Hadrian's Wall was built to keep out which group?
sourceFact: 3.7: 'the Emperor Hadrian built a wall in the north of England to keep out the Picts (ancestors of the Scottish people).'

question: Which three peoples invaded Britain from northern Europe after the Romans left, giving modern English its basis?
options: The Jutes, the Angles and the Saxons
sourceFact: 3.7: 'Britain was again invaded by tribes from northern Europe: the Jutes, the Angles and the Saxons. The languages they spoke are the basis of modern-day English.'

question: Who united the Anglo-Saxon kingdoms in England and defeated the Vikings?
sourceFact: 3.7: 'The Anglo-Saxon kingdoms in England united under King Alfred the Great, who defeated the Vikings.'

question: In what year did the Norman Conquest take place?
sourceFact: 3.7: 'In 1066, an invasion led by William, the Duke of Normandy... defeated Harold, the Saxon king of England, at the Battle of Hastings.'

question: What is the name of the survey William the Conqueror ordered, listing towns, villages, landowners and livestock across England?
sourceFact: 3.7: 'William sent people all over England to draw up lists of all the towns and villages... This was called the Domesday Book.'
